title: First Fridays
hookLine: nine first Fridays of confession and communion, from the Sacred Heart devotion

cards: A parish bulletin, near the bottom, between the bake sale and a reminder about parking: First Friday. Confessions before the morning Mass. Adoration afterward.

Some people circle it. Some keep a small card in a wallet with boxes to tick, month after month, until the boxes run out. It's a devotion with a number built into it, and a promise attached to the number.

teach.b: It begins in a convent in France, with a nun this path has met before, Margaret Mary Alacoque.

In her account, Jesus showed her his heart and asked that people receive communion on the first Friday of each month, in reparation: making up, in love, for the coldness his love so often meets. Why Friday?
The Gospels place the crucifixion on the day of preparation before the Sabbath, the day Christians call Friday.
Every Friday echoes Good Friday, and the first of each month became a small Good Friday on the calendar. Then the promise.

teach.h: NINE IN A ROW: THE GREAT PROMISE.
teach.b: In a letter, Margaret Mary passed on what's known as the great promise: that those who received communion on the first Friday for nine months in a row would not die without the grace of repentance and the sacraments.

That's where the nine comes from. The Church has permitted the devotion and encouraged it. It doesn't teach that nine Fridays work like a ticket; in Catholic teaching, grace is never bought by keeping a schedule.
What the day holds: the devotion asks for communion, and the Church asks anyone aware of serious sin to go to confession before communion. So parishes open the confessional that morning.
Some add an hour of adoration before the Blessed Sacrament, or a litany of the Sacred Heart.
In Matthew, Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you." A first Friday is an appointment with that invitation.
Nine of them, one a month, is a long time to keep showing up. That's part of the point.

how: Catholics who keep the First Friday devotion go to Mass and receive communion on the first Friday of the month, often after confession, in honor of the Sacred Heart; some keep nine in a row, and parishes often add confessions and adoration that day.

games.q: you're a sister in Margaret Mary's convent, and she tells you what she says Jesus asked for on the first Friday of each month. what was it?
o: a fast from all food that day.
communion, in reparation for coldness toward his love.
games.why: communion, in reparation: making up in love for the coldness his love meets. the great promise of the nine Fridays was passed on in one of her letters.

practice: Find, in your head or on your phone, the first Friday of next month, and mark it: a dot, a star, a word.
If you're Catholic and you pray, you might plan to go to Mass that morning, or to confession, or simply stop into a church for a few minutes.
If that isn't your practice, the day can still carry something: an hour kept free, one kindness for someone who's worn out.

wordCard.voice: First Fridays. The first Friday of each month, kept with communion in honor of the Sacred Heart, and, in Margaret Mary's account, kept nine months in a row with a promise attached.

carryVoice: Your line: nine fridays. Each one a small echo of Good Friday. Until tomorrow.
